59fa4bd33bc00227.text: EVIS EUS ENDOSCOPIC ULTRASOUND CENTER OLYMPUS EU-ME3 is intended to be used with Olympus ultrasound endoscopes and Olympus ultrasound probes to observe real-time ultrasound images and is indicated for use within the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, biliary and pancreatic ducts and surrounding organs, intraluminal ultrasound for airways, tracheobronchial tree, trans-rectal, trans-urethral, and trans-esophageal (non-cardiac).

15dd14a541a05547.text: [Modes of Operation] The Modes of Operation are B mode, PWD (Pulsed Wave Doppler) mode, Color Doppler (including Power Doppler) mode, combinations of each mode of operation (B mode, PWD mode, Color Doppler mode) and Other (Harmonic Imaging, Elastography and Shear Wave Speed Measurement [Shear Wave Quantification]).

19501ee403ee8fa9.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use Dual-screen display This function displays two ultrasound images of different modes side by side on the monitor. This is used in PW mode, FLOW mode, ELST, mode, and CHE mode. Stroke The movement range of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Pitch The movement interval of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Live Status where ultrasound transmission is performed and the ultrasound image is displayed in real time. Freeze Status where ultrasound transmission is stopped and the ultrasound image acquired just before is displayed. Release This function records the image displayed on the monitor as a still image on ancillary equipment (e. g. , color video printer). STC (Sensitivity Time Control) This function adjusts the brightness at each distance from the ultrasound transducer. Focal point This is the convergence point of the ultrasound waves to be transmitted. The resolution is better near the focal point. s-FOCUS This function reduces the change in resolution with distance from the ultrasound transducer surface (focus-dependent) by combining the received signals obtained from multiple transmissions (aperture synthesis processing). L. E. reduction (Low Echo reduction) Image processing that suppresses low-level signals in the received signals for reducing noise. Weak signals from the tissue are also suppressed. Structure enhance Image processing that reduces speckle noise while highlighting the boundaries of structures. Smoothing Image processing that spatially smooths ultrasound images.

c8b479519eafc4c6.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use MI (Mechanical Index) An indicator of the ease with which ultrasound can cause mechanical effects on a patient. The higher the MI, the more likely it is to cause mechanical stress/damage on the patient. PIP (Picture-in-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays a small screen within the screen. POP (Picture-out-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays two images side by side. Operation pointer This is a pointer that is displayed on the monitor and used to perform various operations. The operation pointer changes its shape so that it appears as an arrow pointer (white arrow mark) when used on the menu screen, as a measurement mark (“x” mark) when measuring, and as a cursor mark (blinking square mark) when entering comments. Pointer A green arrow mark that appears on the ultrasound image when the POINTER key is pressed. Administrator This is the administrator of the security functions of the Ultrasound Center. When you log into the Ultrasound Center as an administrator, you can register and edit general users, reset passwords, set protected functions, and perform other operations. General user This is a user who uses the Ultrasound Center other than the administrator. To use the protected functions, the user needs to enter the ID and password that were set by the administrator. Tap An action where you touch the trackpad with your fingertip as if tapping it. Swipe An action performed by stroking the trackpad with a single finger. Flick An action where you quickly slide your fingertip on the trackpad. Pinch in An action where you pinch two fingers together on the trackpad.

92615b80de494baa.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use Pinch out An action where you spread two fingers apart on the trackpad. Click Pressing the SET key or tapping the trackpad selects the position indicated by the operation pointer on the screen. Audit log A record of the security status of the EU-ME 3 (status of access to data recorded in the EU-ME 3 and login status). User qualifications This instrument should be used by persons trained in the use of this instrument. If there is an official user qualification standard for performing endoscopy and endoscopic treatment that has been defined by the medical administration or other official bodies, such as professional associations for endoscopy or specialists in endoscopy, you should follow this standard. If there is no official qualification standard, the operator of this instrument must be approved by the medical safety manager of the healthcare facility or person in charge of the department (department of internal medicine, etc. ). The physician should be qualified to operate and perform safely the planned endoscopy and endoscopic treatment following guidelines set by the academic societies on endoscopy, etc. , and considering the difficulty of endoscopy and endoscopic treatment. This manual does not explain or discuss endoscopic procedures. Instrument compatibility Refer to “System chart and Compatible Olympus Ultrasound Endoscopes and Probes” on page 687 to confirm that the Ultrasound Center is compatible with the ancillary equipment being used. Using incompatible equipment may result in patient injury or equipment damage and makes it impossible to obtain the expected functionality. 98ad79b948a0962a.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use Repair and modification The Ultrasound Center does not contain any user-serviceable parts. Do not disassemble, modify, or attempt to repair it; patient or operator injury, equipment damage and/or the impossibility to obtain the expected functionality can result. Some troubles that appear to be malfunctions may be correctable by referring to Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the trouble cannot be resolved using the information in Chapter 11, contact Olympus. This instrument is to be repaired by Olympus technicians only. Olympus is not liable for any injury or damage that occurs as a result of repairs attempted by non-Olympus personnel. Signal words The following signal words are used throughout this manual: Indicates an imminently hazardous situation which, if not avoided, will result in

13c87d18b596fa6e.text: ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.

1adc5a3a6babfea9.text: Important Information — Please Read Before Use Applying ALARA The system imaging mode selected by the ultrasound examiner is determined by the information required. Understanding the nature of the imaging mode being used allows the trained ultrasound examiner to apply the ALARA principle. Prudent use of ultrasound implies that the patient exposure to ultrasound is limited to the lowest output for the shortest time necessary to achieve acceptable diagnostic results. The ultrasound examiner uses the system controls to adjust image quality and ultrasound output. Reference materials (1) Medical Ultrasound Safety, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2014 (2) Acoustic Output Labeling Standard for Diagnostic Ultrasound Equipment, American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine, 2008 (3) IEC 60601-2-37: 2007, IEC 60601-2-37: 2007+A 1: 2015 Medical electrical equipment – part 2 -37: Particular requirements for the basic safety and essential performance of ultrasonic medical diagnostic and monitoring equipment (4) IEC 62359: 2010+A 1: 2017 Ultrasonics – Field characterization – Test methods for the determination of thermal and mechanical indices related to medical diagnostic ultrasonic fields (5) Marketing Clearance of Diagnostic Ultrasound Systems and Transducers, FDA, 2023

a312dd139918e177.text: • Review this chapter thoroughly and prepare the ancillary equipment properly before use. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and also could lead to an electric shock, burn, or fire. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

1 Precautions for inspection

5bc2c82e8f5a2632.text: • Read Chapter 3, “Installation and Connection”, and Chapter 4, “Function Setup”, and properly prepare the equipment to be used. If the equipment is not properly prepared before each use, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to a fire, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, Ch. 5 inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

Also, continued use of the equipment when it is malfunctioning could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, Ch. 5 inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

bae11a0d4f0e0623.text: • Before using, inspect by following the instructions in this chapter. Also, for ancillary equipment used in combination with the Ultrasound Center, inspect by following the instructions in the equipment’s instruction manuals. If anything irregular is found, do not use the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the instructions in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If an irregularity is still observed, contact Olympus. If you continue to use the Ultrasound Center even though something feels irregular, it may not function properly, and it could also lead to an equipment breakdown, electrical shock, burn, or other accident. Also, if the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

6e5936636ee54385.text: • Wear protective equipment such as goggles, face mask, waterproof protective clothing, and chemical-resistant, waterproof gloves with sufficient length. If the equipment malfunctions during a procedure, it could damage the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

1 Precautions for operation

a6d5dcacfe79ad37.text: • If you notice any irregularity during use, immediately stop using the Ultrasound Center, and take corrective action by following the procedure below. Continued use of the Ultrasound Center while it is operating irregularly could harm the health of the patient. If the ultrasound image or endoscopic image is not visible or remains as a still image, and you do not know how to recover it, turn the power off and then back on after about 10 seconds. If using together with ancillary equipment, turn them off and on again by following the instructions in their instruction manuals. If this does not resolve the irregularity, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. If another irregularity is observed, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. After pulling out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope, take corrective action Ch. 6 by following the procedures in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the Ultrasound Center is still not restored to a normal operating state, contact Olympus.

If this does not resolve the irregularity, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. If another irregularity is observed, immediately stop use, and slowly pull out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope from the patient by following the instructions in the instruction manual for the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope. After pulling out the ultrasound endoscope or endoscope, take corrective action Ch. 6 by following the procedures in Chapter 11, “Troubleshooting”. If the Ultrasound Center is still not restored to a normal operating state, contact Olympus.

Doing so could result in malfunctions, electromagnetic noise at a level that could affect observation and procedures on the monitor due to electromagnetic waves, and loss of ultrasound and endoscopic images. If imaging is lost during a procedure, it could result in damage to the patient's tissues and cause bleeding, inflammation, perforation, or other adverse effects.

49a7069a7c532eca.text: Press the [COLOR] button in the FLOW MODE section to set to COLOR FLOW mode. 28314cd089bdc7ed.text: Yellow Direction moving toward the ultrasound transducer surface

f3b81c116aea683d.text: Blue Direction moving away from the ultrasound transducer surface

81378e628376e4af.text: Press the [POWER] button in the FLOW MODE section to set to POWER FLOW mode. In POWER FLOW mode, when blood flow is detected in the ROI, the detected location is displayed in red. The relationship between the displayed color and blood flow strength is shown in Figure 7.59.

7316de36453bdde5.text: Press the [H-FLOW] button in the FLOW MODE section to set to H-FLOW mode. H-FLOW mode displays less protrusion from blood vessels than POWER FLOW mode. 09eb90ac360e5f90.text: 9.1 Summary of user settings The user settings function makes it possible to save parameter values regarding image quality and actions regarding trackpad operations for each user or observation goal. It is possible to register a new entry or edit, copy, or delete existing settings. The user settings saved for each ultrasound endoscope and ultrasound probe at the time of device delivery are referred to as standard settings. User settings newly created or edited and saved by the user are referred to as custom settings. Up to ten custom settings can be registered for each ultrasound endoscope and ultrasound probe, respectively. The notations (classifications) used in the Ultrasound Center, the names of standard settings and the product names of ultrasound endoscopes are shown in Table

5b9ea3bf8d3668dd.text: Mode / Display Settings related to the used mode and display.

8462c0c3400b0b79.text: Image adjust 1 Sets up image adjustment including frequency, gain, and so on for use in B mode.

25d8d165ac0629c6.text: Image adjust 2 Settings related to focus in B mode.

c42a28ce3c405be4.text: Image adjust 3 Settings related to gamma, brightness, and so on in B mode.

d23cf5afa839d5a9.text: Image adjust 4 Settings related to various types of image processing in B mode.

2aeccdeac33fe60c.text: Sets modes used in B mode and items related to display of the B mode screen.

df07b18ba2b874b2.text: Sets up items regarding image adjustment including frequency, gain, and so on for use in B mode.

dc021c4bdda351f6.text: Auto Preset Focus Sets the preset focus for when Focus is auto. Refer to “  Adjust the focus on the FOCUS menu screen.” on page 276 for the method of switching during examination.

2c3102dee24d4579.text: Manual Selects up to two points from the 12 preset focus points when focus adjustment is manual. Refer to “  Adjust the focus on the FOCUS menu screen.” on page 276 for the method of adjusting during examination.

d4a7399903f72d27.text: Sets items related to brightness signal steps, the gamma curve and so on.

672a53672edeaa0a.text: AGC Sets the level for suppressing brightness of high-brightness areas with respect to B mode (common for all frequencies) and THE mode (common for THE-P and THE-R). Refer to ““  AGC” on page 267 for the method of adjusting during examination.

321f24fc507b6712.text: Gray map Sets the signal scales from black to white with respect to B mode (common for all frequencies) and THE mode (common for THE-P and THE-R). Refer to “  Gray map” on page 269 for the method of adjusting during examination.

d7772baad9255151.text: Gamma Curve Selects the curve shape of the input/output characteristics of the brightness signals. Refer to “  Gamma curve and gamma level” on page 268 for the method of adjusting during examination.

b12fd82529311def.text: Gamma Level Sets the level of the size of the gamma curvatures other than linear with respect to B mode (common to all frequencies) and THE mode (common to THE-P and THE-R). Refer to “  Gamma curve and gamma level” on page 268 for the method of adjusting during examination.

713a5253c0097820.text: Color Map Selects the color map for displaying strength and weakness in the ultrasound signal. Cannot be adjusted during examination.

e51bc9201003bdf2.text: Line density Sets scan line density. Refer to “  Scan line density” on page 265 for the method of adjusting during examination.

dc94ae13bce28860.text: Persistence Sets the level of the image processing that temporally smoothen ultrasound images. The higher the level, the smoother the images. Refer to “  Persistence” on page 281 for the method of adjusting during examination.

c46fffe76971fc75.text: Smoothing Sets ON/OFF of the image processing to make the image with good connection. Also, set the processing level of the image processing. The higher the level, the better the image connection. Refer to “  Smoothing” on page 282 for the method of adjusting during examination.

6a60f15400072e98.text: Structure enhance Turns highlighting of structure boundaries and speckle noise reduction image processing on and off. Also sets the processing level for image processing. Refer to “  Structure enhance” on page 279 for the method of adjusting during examination.

0764596cdf2bb8fd.text: Echo enhance Turns image processing that reduces noise while increasing overall image contrast on and off. Also sets the processing level for image processing. Refer to “  Echo enhance” on page 282 for the method of adjusting during examination.

7cb22ca35bcfb886.text: Brightness enhance Turns on and off an image processing feature that maintains the brightness level while increasing image contrast. When on, the processing level can be set. Refer to “  Brightness enhance” on page 284 for the method of adjusting during examination.

b93979dd9b13453d.text: It is possible to set and save the size of the ROI used in TIC analysis and the rendering method for TIC analysis graphs. The TIC analysis settings already saved on the Ultrasound Center, are referred to as the TIC standard settings. TIC analysis settings newly registered or edited by the user are referred to as TIC custom settings, and up to 10 of these can be saved. 2c4872370a5adcc9.text: • It is the responsibility of the operator to understand the risk of the output of the Ultrasound Center, and to act appropriately in order to obtain the needed diagnostic information with the minimum risk to the patient. To be able to do so, we describe interpretation of the displayed ultrasonic exposure parameters, Thermal Index and Mechanical Index.
lists: It is the responsibility of the operator to understand the risk of the output of the Ultrasound Center, and to act appropriately in order to obtain the needed diagnostic information with the minimum risk to the patient. To be able to do so, we describe interpretation of the displayed ultrasonic exposure parameters, Thermal Index and Mechanical Index.

04dc516a56ba08ea.text: • The relationship of various acoustic output parameters (for example, acoustic intensity, acoustic pressure, power, etc. ) to biological endpoints is not presently fully understood. Evidence to date has identified two fundamental mechanisms, thermal and mechanical, by which ultrasound may induce bioeffects in certain cases alteration or damage to tissue.
lists: The relationship of various acoustic output parameters (for example, acoustic intensity, acoustic pressure, power, etc. ) to biological endpoints is not presently fully understood. Evidence to date has identified two fundamental mechanisms, thermal and mechanical, by which ultrasound may induce bioeffects in certain cases alteration or damage to tissue.

49532229463d7853.text: • The temperature rise and the possibility of cavitation seem to depend on such factors as the total energy output, the mode, the shape of the ultrasound beam, the position of the focus, the center frequency, the shape of the waveform, the pulse repetition frequency, and the duty factor. The TI and MI are indices designed to give the user instant information about the potential for thermal or mechanical bioeffects. Because the MI and TI indices reflect instantaneous output conditions, they do not take into account the cumulative effects (especially heating) of the total examination time. It is relevant to indicate that shortening insonation times can give a large safety margin under some conditions (wide, scanning beams in soft tissue) but no significant margin under other conditions (narrow, non-scanning beams on bone)
lists: The temperature rise and the possibility of cavitation seem to depend on such factors as the total energy output, the mode, the shape of the ultrasound beam, the position of the focus, the center frequency, the shape of the waveform, the pulse repetition frequency, and the duty factor. The TI and MI are indices designed to give the user instant information about the potential for thermal or mechanical bioeffects. Because the MI and TI indices reflect instantaneous output conditions, they do not take into account the cumulative effects (especially heating) of the total examination time. It is relevant to indicate that shortening insonation times can give a large safety margin under some conditions (wide, scanning beams in soft tissue) but no significant margin under other conditions (narrow, non-scanning beams on bone)

0ac8bd578f21f597.text: • The MI is intended to give a relative indication of the potential for mechanical bioeffects such as cavitation.
lists: The MI is intended to give a relative indication of the potential for mechanical bioeffects such as cavitation.

755bf71e51098397.text: • The TI gives a relative indication of the potential for temperature increase at a specific point along the ultrasound beam. The reason for the term “relative” is that the assumed conditions for heating in tissue are so complex that any single index or model cannot be expected to give the actual increase in temperature for all possible conditions and tissue types. Thus, for a particular beamshape, a TI of 2 represents a higher temperature rise than a TI of 1, but does not necessarily represent a rise of 2C. The important point about the TI is that it is designed to make the operator aware of the possible temperature rise at a particular point in tissue.

Thus, for a particular beamshape, a TI of 2 represents a higher temperature rise than a TI of 1, but does not necessarily represent a rise of 2C. The important point about the TI is that it is designed to make the operator aware of the possible temperature rise at a particular point in tissue.

0f20bef4a2bd60f9.text: • What the indices do provide is an indication of the conditions that are more likely than others to produce thermal and/or mechanical effects.
lists: What the indices do provide is an indication of the conditions that are more likely than others to produce thermal and/or mechanical effects.

99122df44300e42c.text: • The modeling for predicting TI assumes some cooling by blood perfusion. For applications where poorly perfused tissues are expected, the TI may underestimate the possible worst-case temperature rise, and again the TI should be maintained at a lower value. App. Conversely, when scanning organs known to be well perfused, such as hepatic, cardiac or vascular structures, the value of TI may overestimate the temperature rise.

Examples are for breast scanning, when ribs may be exposed, and for vascular studies when vessels lie close to bone surfaces. 732

This assumption may not be universally true, and for this reason TI values in both B-mode and Doppler imaging modes in second and third trimester scanning must be interpreted with caution.

No correction is made for the heating of the transducer itself. The same is true for transcranial transducers and smaller unscanned transducers where the heating is also predicted next to the transducer.

safety_blocks.text: Dual-screen display This function displays two ultrasound images of different modes side by side on the monitor. This is used in PW mode, FLOW mode, ELST, mode, and CHE mode. Stroke The movement range of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Pitch The movement interval of helical scanning in the direction of the insertion axis. Live Status where ultrasound transmission is performed and the ultrasound image is displayed in real time. Freeze Status where ultrasound transmission is stopped and the ultrasound image acquired just before is displayed. Release This function records the image displayed on the monitor as a still image on ancillary equipment (e. g. , color video printer). STC (Sensitivity Time Control) This function adjusts the brightness at each distance from the ultrasound transducer. Focal point This is the convergence point of the ultrasound waves to be transmitted. The resolution is better near the focal point. s-FOCUS This function reduces the change in resolution with distance from the ultrasound transducer surface (focus-dependent) by combining the received signals obtained from multiple transmissions (aperture synthesis processing).

safety_blocks.text: MI (Mechanical Index) An indicator of the ease with which ultrasound can cause mechanical effects on a patient. The higher the MI, the more likely it is to cause mechanical stress/damage on the patient. PIP (Picture-in-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays a small screen within the screen. POP (Picture-out-Picture) This is one of the methods to display endoscopic and ultrasound images simultaneously on the monitor. It displays two images side by side. Operation pointer This is a pointer that is displayed on the monitor and used to perform various operations. The operation pointer changes its shape so that it appears as an arrow pointer (white arrow mark) when used on the menu screen, as a measurement mark (“x” mark) when measuring, and as a cursor mark (blinking square mark) when entering comments. Pointer A green arrow mark that appears on the ultrasound image when the POINTER key is pressed. Administrator This is the administrator of the security functions of the Ultrasound Center. When you log into the Ultrasound Center as an administrator, you can register and edit general users, reset passwords, set protected functions, and perform other operations. General user This is a user who uses the Ultrasound Center other than the administrator. To use the protected functions, the user needs to enter the ID and password that were set by the administrator. Tap An action where you touch the trackpad with your fingertip as if tapping it. Swipe An action performed by stroking the trackpad with a single finger. Flick An action where you quickly slide your fingertip on the trackpad. Pinch in An action where you pinch two fingers together on the trackpad.

Customer should use genuine devices as ancillary equipment for combination of this instrument, considering leakage of personal information and falsification of data by outsider. Follow the facility security policy (ies) for storage and management of this instrument. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.
